newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - Dec 5.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - Dec 5.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Thursday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The Constitutional Court on Wednesday unanimously approved the revised constitution which will be signed by President Nelson Mandela in Sharpeville on Human Rights Day next week.

- Tertiary education institutions could soon be subject to quicker and easier state intervention in campus crises in terms of draft government policy on higher education approved by the cabinet on Wednesday.
- Government is expected to begin retrenching public servants next year after its efforts to cut staff numbers through voluntary severance packages failed to produce meaningful results.

- President Nelson Mandela reaffirmed government's decision to break diplomatic ties with Taiwan during a meeting on Wednesday with the country's Foreign Minister John Chang who is understood to have asked for a two-year extension of the phase-down of formal relations.
- The gold price confounded expectations on Wednesday when it rose, pushing the JSE's all gold index higher as investors piled in to snap up South African gold shares.

- Pick 'n Pay and 7-Eleven, the Cape-based retailers, will move into Gauteng next month in a joint venture to open the first of about 40 franchised convenience stores planned for the province by the end of next year.
- Telkom said on Wednesday that attributable income in the six months to September 30 rose 26 percent to 664.2 million rand, fuelled by revenue which increased 24 pecent to 7.9 billion rand.
- Capital Alliance and Saflife, its holding company, will acquire Seeff Holdings, the property group in an 86 million rand deal.
- South Africa's new constitution is set to come into force in February, before the start of the new parliamentary session, political sources said on Wednesday.
- Gauteng safety and security officials and the National Party are embroiled in a war of words over crime statistics released on Wednesday by MEC Jessie Duarte's office.

- The number of car hijackings in Gauteng has dropped, according to new statistics supplied by the Gauteng Department of Safety and Security. The latest "updated, analysed, contextualised and correct" figures in a Gauteng police report released on November 14 had shown a drop in the number of hijackings by 544 cases when compared to the figures in the same period a year ago.
